A layer lay over the viewport when the page was read (div#elementor-popup-modal-4697, on top at 78% of the points sampled: a consent backdrop, a dialog): it was hidden while images, labels and contrast were captured, so the pixels measured are the page's own.

3 frame(s) were checked by axe-core only: their content is not in the snapshot (another origin, or it loaded after the page was read), so Rampa's rules and the judged criteria did not read it: html > body > footer > section:nth-of-type(1) > div > div > div > section > div > div:nth-of-type(1) > div > div:nth-of-type(3) > div > div > iframe (https://maps.google.com/maps?q=Rua%20Ranulfo%20%C3%81lvares%2C%201620%20Governador%20Valadares&t=m&z=14&output=embed&iwloc=near), html > body > footer > section:nth-of-type(1) > div > div > div > section > div > div:nth-of-type(2) > div > div:nth-of-type(3) > div > div > iframe (https://maps.google.com/maps?q=Rua%20B%C3%A1rbara%20Heliodora%2C%201360%20Governador%20Valadares&t=m&z=14&output=embed&iwloc=near), html > body > footer > section:nth-of-type(1) > div > div > div > section > div > div:nth-of-type(3) > div > div:nth-of-type(3) > div > div > iframe (https://maps.google.com/maps?q=Rua%20Ranulfo%20%C3%81lvares%2C%201620%20Governador%20Valadares&t=m&z=14&output=embed&iwloc=near).

7 image(s) were left without a capture, so no judgment looked at them: 1 outside the page (an off-canvas menu); 2 cut off by the box that holds it; 4 over the limit of images captured per page. The snapshot says why for each (native.imageSkipped).
